fix_commit.message: vtls: avoid NULL deref on bad PEM input
fix_commit.author: Daniel Stenberg

findings.title: NULL pointer dereference in pubkey_pem_to_der() on empty PEM body
findings.message: pubkey_pem_to_der() strips newlines/CRs from the base64 body found between the '-----BEGIN PUBLIC KEY-----' and '-----END PUBLIC KEY-----' markers by appending each non-newline character into a dynbuf (pbuf) via Curl_dyn_addn(). If the PEM content between the markers consists solely of '\n'/'\r' characters (or is empty), Curl_dyn_addn() is never called, so pbuf's internal buffer (bufr) is never allocated and remains NULL. The code then unconditionally calls 'Curl_base64_decode(Curl_dyn_ptr(&pbuf), der, der_len)'. Curl_dyn_ptr() simply returns s->bufr, i.e. NULL in this case, which is then passed as the source string into the base64 decoder, which dereferences it (e.g. to compute strlen/read characters), causing a NULL pointer dereference. This is reachable via CURLOPT_PINNEDPUBLICKEY when an attacker-controlled or malformed PEM-format public key file/pinned key value is supplied that contains an empty or whitespace-only body between the BEGIN/END markers.
findings.suggestion: Before calling Curl_base64_decode(), check whether any data was actually written into pbuf (e.g. via Curl_dyn_len(&pbuf) == 0) and return CURLE_BAD_CONTENT_ENCODING in that case instead of passing a possibly-NULL pointer into the decoder.

ground_truth.root_cause: When pubkey_pem_to_der() was converted from a fixed malloc'd buffer (which was always allocated to at least 1 byte, guaranteeing a valid, if empty, C string) to a lazily-allocated dynbuf (struct dynbuf), the code failed to account for the case where zero bytes are ever appended to the dynbuf. In that case Curl_dyn_ptr()/curlx_dyn_ptr() legitimately returns NULL (mirroring the dynbuf's internal unallocated state), but the caller did not check for this before handing the pointer to the base64 decoder.

must_cover.reason: Primary location of finding: NULL pointer dereference in pubkey_pem_to_der() on empty PEM body
